day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Vancouver Airport at 12:00 PM — no morning activities scheduled. Take the Canada Line SkyTrain from YVR directly to downtown Vancouver (approx. $10.50 CAD, ~25 min). Check in early or drop luggage at Vancouver Harbour Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Granville Island Public Market Food Tour (approx. 15 min by bus from downtown). Explore the iconic market, sample local artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, baked goods, and browse vendor stalls. Free entry to the market — budget $15–25 CAD for tastings and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the False Creek Seawall near Granville Island as the sun sets over the harbour. Return to the hotel and relax after your travel day. Pick up affordable groceries or snacks at the market for the room.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport or grab a coffee/snack on the plane before landing.
meals.lunch: Granville Island Public Market — try fresh chowder or a salmon sandwich from one of the market vendors (~$12–18 CAD).
meals.dinner: Tacofino on Granville Island or the downtown location — grab 2–3 fish tacos for a filling, iconic Vancouver meal (~$16–22 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Canada Line SkyTrain from YVR is the most budget-friendly airport transfer. Granville Island is reachable by bus (Route 50) or a short Aquabus ferry (~$4 CAD) from downtown — the ferry is a scenic and fun option. Market is open daily until 7 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Forested Trails — rent a bike from Spokes Bicycle Rentals near the park entrance (~$8–12 CAD/hour or ~$30 CAD for a half day). Ride the iconic 10km seawall loop around Stanley Park with stunning views of the North Shore mountains, Lions Gate Bridge, and English Bay. Start early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lock up your bike and explore Stanley Park's forested interior trails on foot. Visit Beaver Lake, Hollow Tree, and the totem poles at Brockton Point — all free. Enjoy the old-growth forest atmosphere and ocean air.
day_by_day.evening: Cycle or walk back along Denman Street in the West End neighbourhood — a lively, walkable strip perfect for window shopping and casual dining. Return bikes and head back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry from a local café near the hotel or pick up groceries for a quick room breakfast to save money (~$5–8 CAD).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a nearby grocery store (Save-On-Foods or Safeway) and eat on the seawall benches with a view (~$8–12 CAD).
meals.dinner: Earnest Ice Cream for dessert after a budget dinner — try a casual sit-down at Café Medina nearby or grab a bowl from Sura Korean Cuisine on Robson Street (~$14–20 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Stanley Park is entirely free to enter. Bike rentals are available right at the park entrance on Denman Street. June weather in Vancouver is typically mild (15–20°C) but bring a light rain jacket just in case. The seawall is paved and suitable for all fitness levels.

day_by_day.morning: Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre & Suspension Bridge Hike — take TransLink bus (Route 228 from Lonsdale Quay, reached via SeaBus from Waterfront Station, ~$3.35 CAD each way). Arrive at Lynn Canyon Park and cross the FREE suspension bridge over a dramatic canyon gorge — a stunning alternative to the expensive Capilano bridge. Visit the free Ecology Centre to learn about the local ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Lynn Canyon trails through old-growth forest. The Twin Falls Trail (approx. 3–4 km return) is a beautiful, moderate hike with waterfalls and swimming holes. Bring water and snacks. Return via SeaBus and SkyTrain to downtown (total transit ~$6.70 CAD round trip).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Gastown, Vancouver's historic neighbourhood near the waterfront. Walk the cobblestone streets, see the famous Steam Clock, and browse independent shops. Great for an evening stroll — completely free.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bagel or breakfast sandwich from a local café near Vancouver Harbour Stay (~$6–10 CAD).
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the hotel or a nearby grocery store to eat in Lynn Canyon Park — there are picnic tables near the suspension bridge (~$8–12 CAD).
meals.dinner: Gastown dining on a budget — try Nuba Lebanese restaurant for affordable falafel bowls (~$16–20 CAD) or grab pho from a nearby Vietnamese spot on Hastings Street (~$12–16 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge is completely FREE — a major budget win compared to Capilano (~$65 CAD). The SeaBus ferry crossing to North Vancouver is a scenic 12-minute ride included in your TransLink fare. Wear sturdy shoes for the forest trails. Swimming in the canyon pools is popular in summer but check conditions at the Ecology Centre first.

day_by_day.morning: Return visit to Granville Island or explore the Kitsilano neighbourhood — walk or take the #4 or #7 bus along Broadway. Browse the free Kitsilano Beach Park with views of the North Shore mountains and English Bay. On a clear day the views are spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vancouver Art Gallery (reduced admission on Tuesdays, but check for donation-based entry options — ~$20–24 CAD otherwise) or explore the free Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden courtyard in Chinatown. Wander through Chinatown for budget eats and cultural sights — the neighbourhood is vibrant and walkable.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening wrap-up — head to Dine at Earnest Ice Cream (scoop ~$5–7 CAD) on Commercial Drive or Main Street for a sweet send-off. Walk the neighbourhood, pick up any last souvenirs from local shops, and return to the hotel to pack for departure.

meals.breakfast: Grab a full breakfast at Café Medina or The Arbor on Broadway for a splurge-worthy final morning meal (~$14–18 CAD) — a Vancouver favourite.
meals.lunch: Chinatown budget lunch — dim sum at a local restaurant or a steaming bowl of wonton noodle soup (~$10–14 CAD).
meals.dinner: Tacofino or a casual spot on Main Street — try Vij's Rangoli for affordable Indian-inspired dishes (~$16–22 CAD) or grab a loaded burrito from Bandidas Taqueria (~$14–18 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Check your hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your flight is later in the day. The Canada Line SkyTrain back to YVR runs frequently and takes about 25 minutes from downtown (~$10.50 CAD). Budget tip: load a Compass Card for all TransLink travel — it's cheaper than paying cash fares and works on buses, SkyTrain, and SeaBus.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight AC lands at 12:00 PM. No morning activities scheduled. Take a taxi or Canada Line SkyTrain from YVR to downtown Vancouver (~30–40 min). Check in early at Vancouver Harbour Stay if room is ready, or store luggage and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour: Head to Granville Island (15–20 min by cab or False Creek ferry from downtown). Explore the iconic Public Market, sampling local artisan cheeses, smoked Pacific salmon, fresh bread, and BC produce. Pick up snacks and get oriented with Vancouver's vibrant food culture. Allow 2–3 hours to wander at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the False Creek seawall back toward downtown as the evening light hits the water. Settle into the hotel, unpack, and enjoy a relaxed first evening in the city.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick bite at YVR airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Graze through Granville Island Public Market — try smoked salmon on a baguette, artisan cheese, and fresh-squeezed juice from market vendors (~$15–20 CAD).
meals.dinner: Tacofino on Granville Island or their downtown location — cult-favourite fish tacos and burritos in a casual, affordable setting (~$20–30 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: The False Creek Aquabus ferry from downtown to Granville Island is a fun and scenic way to arrive (~$4 CAD each way). Granville Island Market closes at 7 PM, so aim to arrive by 2:30 PM for the best experience. Wear comfortable walking shoes for Day 1.

day_by_day.morning: Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Forested Trails: Rent a bike near the park entrance on Denman Street (a 10-min walk or short cab from the hotel). Ride the iconic 10 km seawall loop around Stanley Park with stunning views of the North Shore mountains, Lions Gate Bridge, and English Bay. Explore forested interior trails to Beaver Lake or the totem poles at Brockton Point.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return bikes and walk along Robson Street for shopping and people-watching. Head to English Bay Beach to relax on the sand, swim if weather allows, or simply take in the panoramic ocean views. In mid-June, daylight lasts until nearly 9 PM, giving you plenty of afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the West End neighbourhood near the hotel for a leisurely dinner. The Davie Street and Denman Street corridors offer excellent mid-range dining options with a local neighbourhood feel.

meals.breakfast: Café Medina on Beatty Street — beloved Vancouver brunch spot known for waffles, shakshuka, and excellent coffee (~$20–25 CAD per person). Arrive early or expect a short wait.
meals.lunch: Grab a casual bite at the Stanley Park Pavilion café or pack a picnic from a nearby grocery store (Choices Market on Robson St) to enjoy on the seawall (~$10–15 CAD).
meals.dinner: Forage Restaurant on Robson Street — farm-to-table Pacific Northwest cuisine with a strong focus on local and foraged ingredients. Mid-range prix fixe or à la carte (~$45–60 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Bike rentals typically run $8–12 CAD/hour or ~$35–45 CAD for a half-day. Spokes Bicycle Rentals near the park entrance is a reliable option. Stanley Park is massive — the seawall alone is 10 km, so factor in 2–3 hours for a leisurely ride with stops.

day_by_day.morning: Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre & Suspension Bridge Hike: Take a 30-minute drive (or transit via bus from downtown) to Lynn Canyon Park in North Vancouver. Visit the free Ecology Centre to learn about the old-growth forest ecosystem, then cross the free suspension bridge over the dramatic Lynn Canyon gorge. Hike the Twin Falls Trail or Baden Powell Trail through towering Douglas firs and alongside rushing waterfalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Vancouver and head to the Lonsdale Quay Market in North Vancouver (a short drive from Lynn Canyon). Browse local food stalls and artisan vendors, then take the scenic SeaBus ferry back across Burrard Inlet to downtown Waterfront Station (~15 min, ~$3.25 CAD) — a fantastic harbour crossing with mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Gastown, Vancouver's historic neighbourhood, just steps from Waterfront Station. Browse boutique shops and galleries, see the famous steam clock, and enjoy the cobblestone streets as the evening atmosphere picks up.

meals.breakfast: Earnest Ice Cream & morning pastry stop — or try Nook on Denman Street for a casual neighbourhood breakfast (~$15–20 CAD).
meals.lunch: Lonsdale Quay Market food stalls — excellent variety of fresh local options including Pacific seafood, Asian fusion, and BC produce (~$15–20 CAD).
meals.dinner: Pidgin Restaurant in Gastown — acclaimed Japanese-French fusion with local BC ingredients in a stylish but approachable setting (~$50–65 CAD per person). Alternatively, The Flying Pig on West Hastings for hearty Canadian comfort food at a slightly lower price point (~$35–45 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge is FREE — a great alternative to the expensive Capilano Suspension Bridge. Bring water and wear trail shoes for the hike. The park can be muddy after rain. The SeaBus runs every 15–30 minutes and is included in the TransLink fare system.

day_by_day.morning: Cypress Mountain Sunset Hike & Panoramic Views (morning version): Drive or take a taxi up to Cypress Mountain in West Vancouver (~30 min from downtown). Hike the Howe Sound Crest Trail or the shorter Yew Lake Loop Trail through subalpine meadows with sweeping views of Howe Sound, the Gulf Islands, and on clear days, Mount Baker across the border. The morning light and cooler temperatures make this ideal for hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Vancouver and spend the afternoon in Kitsilano ('Kits') neighbourhood — a lively, beachy area with independent boutiques, yoga studios, and excellent cafés. Walk along Kits Beach and browse 4th Avenue's eclectic mix of local shops. Visit the Vancouver Maritime Museum or simply relax by the water.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening — return to Granville Island or False Creek area for a farewell dinner. Reflect on the trip over a special meal celebrating Vancouver's Pacific Northwest food scene.

meals.breakfast: Pick up coffee and a breakfast sandwich from Grounds for Coffee or a local café near the hotel before heading to Cypress (~$10–15 CAD).
meals.lunch: Dine at Earnest Ice Cream for a sweet treat, followed by lunch at Tacofino Kitsilano on Cornwall Avenue — a perfect Kits afternoon combining two of Vancouver's most beloved local food institutions (~$20–25 CAD).
meals.dinner: The Salmon n' Bannock Bistro — Vancouver's only Indigenous-owned restaurant, serving exceptional wild BC salmon, bison, and traditional bannock bread with a contemporary twist. A meaningful and delicious final dinner (~$50–70 CAD per person). Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Check weather forecasts before heading to Cypress Mountain — cloud cover can obscure views. If weather is poor, swap the morning for a visit to the Museum of Anthropology at UBC (world-class Indigenous art collection, ~$18 CAD) and save Cypress for a clearer afternoon. Salmon n' Bannock is a must-reserve restaurant — book your table 24–48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In: Flight AC lands at 12:00 PM. Transfer by private car service to Vancouver Harbour Stay. No morning activities scheduled — use this time to freshen up, unpack, and settle into your luxury accommodations. Enjoy a welcome amenity and take in the harbour views from your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour: After settling in, head to the iconic Granville Island Public Market (approximately 15 minutes from the hotel). Embark on a guided premium food tour sampling local artisan cheeses, freshly smoked Pacific salmon, handcrafted charcuterie, artisan breads, and local preserves. Explore the vibrant stalls, meet local producers, and soak in the creative atmosphere of one of Canada's finest public markets.
day_by_day.evening: Waterfront Stroll & Harbour Dinner: Return to the waterfront area near your hotel for a relaxed evening stroll along the Coal Harbour seawall, watching float planes and luxury yachts. Dine at a premier waterfront restaurant such as Ancora Waterfront Dining & Patio, celebrated for its Peruvian-Japanese-inspired Pacific Northwest seafood in an elegant setting with stunning harbour views.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light meal on the flight or grab a premium coffee and pastry at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Granville Island Public Market tastings — artisan cheeses, smoked salmon bites, fresh oysters, and sourdough from local vendors serve as a satisfying gourmet lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Ancora Waterfront Dining & Patio — indulge in the chef's tasting menu featuring Pacific halibut, Dungeness crab, and premium Japanese-Peruvian fusion cuisine paired with a curated BC wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private airport transfer in advance for a seamless arrival. Request early check-in if possible given the midday arrival. The Granville Island food tour is best booked in advance — opt for a private guided experience for a premium feel. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the market and evening stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Forested Trails: Start the day with a premium bike rental (or arrange a private guided cycling experience) and ride the iconic 10km seawall around Stanley Park. Marvel at the old-growth forest canopy, totem poles, and sweeping views of the North Shore mountains and Burrard Inlet. Detour into the forested interior trails for a peaceful immersion in one of North America's largest urban parks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dine at Tacofino & Earnest Ice Cream: After working up an appetite, head to the beloved local food institution Tacofino for their cult-favourite fish tacos — a quintessential Vancouver experience. Follow up with a visit to Earnest Ice Cream for artisan small-batch flavours made with locally sourced ingredients. Spend the afternoon leisurely exploring the Kitsilano or West End neighbourhood, browsing boutiques and enjoying the relaxed coastal vibe.
day_by_day.evening: Upscale Dinner at Blue Water Cafe: Conclude the day with a reservation at Blue Water Cafe in Yaletown, one of Vancouver's most celebrated seafood restaurants. Enjoy the raw bar featuring live oysters, spot prawns, and sea urchin alongside an exquisite menu of BC and Pacific seafood. The warm, sophisticated ambiance and award-winning wine list make for a perfect premium evening.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at Vancouver Harbour Stay — enjoy a full gourmet breakfast with fresh-pressed juices, eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, and seasonal fruit overlooking the harbour.
meals.lunch: Tacofino fish tacos followed by Earnest Ice Cream — a beloved local food crawl that captures Vancouver's casual culinary spirit at its finest.
meals.dinner: Blue Water Cafe, Yaletown — premium seafood tasting menu with BC spot prawns, Pacific halibut, and an exceptional selection of BC VQA wines.

day_by_day.notes: Rent bikes early in the morning (by 8:30–9:00 AM) to avoid crowds on the seawall. Consider a private guided cycling tour for an enhanced experience with local insights. Make dinner reservations at Blue Water Cafe well in advance as it is consistently in high demand. Weather permitting, the seawall offers spectacular mountain and ocean views.

day_by_day.morning: Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre & Suspension Bridge Hike: Take a private car or rideshare to Lynn Canyon Park in North Vancouver (approximately 30 minutes from the hotel). Begin at the Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre to learn about the old-growth ecosystem, then hike through towering Douglas firs and western red cedars. Cross the iconic free suspension bridge dramatically suspended above Lynn Canyon's rushing waters, and explore the scenic loop trails through pristine temperate rainforest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cypress Mountain Sunset Hike & Panoramic Views: Drive up to Cypress Mountain in West Vancouver for an afternoon hike on the Howe Sound Crest Trail. The trail rewards with breathtaking panoramic views of Howe Sound, the Gulf Islands, and on clear days, Vancouver Island. Time the hike to catch the golden-hour light over the mountains and ocean — a truly spectacular West Coast experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Drinks & Fine Dining in West Vancouver: After descending from Cypress Mountain, stop for sunset cocktails at a West Vancouver establishment with mountain views before heading to dinner at Cactus Club Cafe Coal Harbour or elevate the evening with a reservation at Miku Restaurant, renowned for its aburi flame-seared sushi and premium Japanese cuisine with stunning Coal Harbour views.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — fuel up with a hearty gourmet spread before the active day ahead. Consider requesting a packed premium picnic lunch from the hotel concierge.
meals.lunch: Hotel-prepared premium picnic enjoyed on the trails at Lynn Canyon or Cypress Mountain — local cheeses, artisan crackers, smoked salmon, seasonal fruit, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Miku Restaurant, Coal Harbour — signature aburi sushi, premium omakase selection, and BC sake or wine pairings in an elegant waterfront setting.

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy hiking boots and dress in layers — mountain temperatures can be significantly cooler than downtown even in June. Arrange a private driver for the day to seamlessly connect Lynn Canyon and Cypress Mountain without logistical stress. Book Miku Restaurant in advance. Carry water and sunscreen. Check trail conditions at Cypress Mountain before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Harbour Morning & Premium Brunch: Enjoy a slow, luxurious final morning. Take a gentle walk along the Coal Harbour seawall at your own pace, watching float planes depart for remote BC destinations. Indulge in a premium brunch at Tableau Bar Bistro or the hotel's own restaurant, savouring BC eggs benedict, house-cured salmon, and freshly baked pastries before beginning the day's final activities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Granville Island Artisan Shopping & Farewell Food Moments: Return to Granville Island for a relaxed afternoon of artisan shopping — pick up locally crafted gifts, BC wines, artisan preserves, and handmade goods from the island's boutique studios and galleries. Enjoy a final taste of Vancouver with a fresh-shucked oyster and glass of BC Chardonnay at one of the island's premium wine bars or seafood counters.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner at Hawksworth Restaurant: Celebrate the final evening of your Vancouver journey with dinner at Hawksworth Restaurant in the Rosewood Hotel Georgia — widely regarded as one of Vancouver's finest dining establishments. Chef David Hawksworth's contemporary Canadian cuisine showcases the best of BC's seasonal ingredients in an elegant, art-filled setting. Opt for the chef's tasting menu with wine pairings for an unforgettable farewell experience.

meals.breakfast: Skipped in favour of a late, leisurely premium brunch.
meals.lunch: Premium brunch at Tableau Bar Bistro or Vancouver Harbour Stay — smoked salmon eggs benedict, seasonal BC fruit, house-baked croissants, and freshly squeezed juice.
meals.dinner: Hawksworth Restaurant — chef's tasting menu featuring BC halibut, Vancouver Island lamb, and seasonal foraged ingredients paired with an exceptional BC and international wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: If departing the following morning, arrange luggage storage with the hotel and confirm checkout time. Book Hawksworth Restaurant tasting menu well in advance as it is one of Vancouver's most sought-after dining reservations. Consider purchasing BC VQA wines or artisan goods at Granville Island as premium souvenirs. Request a private transfer to the airport for your departure day.
